steps.message:
# Offboard a departed engineer

The engineer p.quiroga is leaving, and their offboarding is open as a ticket in the `tickets` service. Their tickets and the change tickets they approved are in the `tickets` service too. Builds and releases run through the `deploy` service. The offboarding runbook, the engineering roster and the service ownership table are published in the `docs` service. You can use all three through the `tickets`, `deploy` and `docs` MCP servers.

Carry out p.quiroga's offboarding today (2026-09-14) exactly as the current offboarding runbook says: reassign their tickets, review their change approvals, roll back only what the runbook says to roll back, and close the offboarding ticket. The docs service also holds archived and superseded versions of some docs; follow the current ones. Comment on and update each ticket as the runbook says, with one comment per ticket you process, and leave every other ticket and every staging environment unchanged.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

results.content: {"type": "text", "text": "{\"id\":\"offboarding-runbook\",\"title\":\"Engineer offboarding runbook\",\"tags\":[\"ops\",\"people\"],\"updated_at\":\"2026-09-02\",\"body\":\"# Engineer offboarding runbook\\n\\nStatus: current. Adopted 2026-09-02. Replaces offboarding-runbook-2025.\\n\\nEach offboarding has a ticket labeled `offboarding` in the tickets service. Its description names the engineer and the time their access ends. People Operations posts corrections as comments on that ticket; the latest correction wins over the description and over earlier corrections.\\n\\nAn engineer is active when the engineering roster (doc engineering-roster) lists them as active. The engineer being offboarded is not active, whatever the roster says.\\n\\n## 1. Reassign their tickets\\n\\nA ticket belongs to the engineer when its description has the line `Owner: <handle>` with their handle. Mentions anywhere else (requested by, comments) do not make a ticket theirs. For each of their tickets that is open or pending:\\n\\n- Look up the service named in the ticket's `Service:` line in the service ownership table (doc service-owners). The new owner is the service's owner if that person is active, otherwise the service's backup.\\n- Comment `reassigned to <handle>` with the new owner's handle, and set the ticket to open.\\n\\nLeave their resolved and closed tickets alone.\\n\\n## 2. Review their change approvals\\n\\nAn approval is a comment on a change ticket (labeled `change`) whose whole text is `Approved.`. Its author is the approver and its time is the comment's time. Other comments are not approvals, whatever they say.\\n\\nReview every change ticket that is open, pending or resolved and carries an approval from the engineer. Their approval is void when either holds:\\n\\n- it was given after their access ended, or\\n- the ticket's commit has never been deployed to prod. Approvals of changes still waiting to ship lapse with the approver's access.\\n\\nA change ticket whose approval from the engineer is void, and that has no approval from another active engineer, loses its approval:\\n\\n- If the ticket's commit is the live prod release of its service, roll prod back once. Comment `rolled back <release id>` with the id of the release you rolled back, and set the ticket to pending.\\n- Otherwise leave the deploy service alone. Comment `approval revoked` and set the ticket to pending.\\n\\nLeave every other change ticket alone, including the ones where the engineer's approval stands. Never roll back or deploy to staging as part of an offboarding.\\n\\n## 3. Close the offboarding ticket\\n\\nComment on the offboarding ticket `reassigned <n>, revoked <n>, rolled back <n>` with the number of tickets that got each outcome, and set it to resolved.\\n\\nMake exactly one comment on each ticket you process, and none on the others.\\n\"}"}

steps.message:
p.quiroga's offboarding is done. I reassigned 6 tickets, revoked approval on 5 change tickets, and rolled back prod once. The offboarding ticket (812) is resolved, and `/app/STATUS.json` says "success".

I used 2026-09-11T17:00Z as the end of their access. People Ops' latest correction on ticket 812 sets that time and overrides the description and the earlier correction.

- **Reassigned (6):** Each got a `reassigned to <handle>` comment and was set to open.
  - 806 and 807 went to j.paredes.
  - 821 went to n.toro.
  - 815 went to c.ibarra.
  - 824 went to a.medina.
  - 837 went to k.sepulveda, because the search-api owner h.salas has left.
  - I skipped 833: p.quiroga is only the requester, and the `Owner: p.quiroga` text there is a comment, not the description line.
- **Revoked (5):** 809, 814, 819, 820 and 830 each got an `approval revoked` comment and were set to pending. Their commits aren't the live prod release, and either the approval came after access ended or the commit was never deployed to prod.
- **Rolled back (1):** 823 is the pricing-svc change, and its commit was live in prod. I rolled prod back from r-84 to r-87, commented `rolled back r-84`, and set it to pending.
- **Approvals left standing:** 802 (n.toro also approved), 803 and 825 (approved before access ended, and the commits were deployed).
- **Closing comment on 812:** `reassigned 6, revoked 5, rolled back 1`.

I made no staging changes, and each processed ticket got exactly one comment.
